title: Now That Jensen is Back, Should You Buy Nvidia Stock Instead of Broadcom Stock? | NVDA Stock vs AVGO
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions.
summary: After Monday's relief rally on Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO faded into Tuesday-Wednesday selling, Parkevtate compares Nvidia and Broadcom head to head to decide which is the better buy. On earnings growth, analysts expect Broadcom at 55% a year and Nvidia at 49% a year over the next several years. On profitability, Nvidia's operating margin is 66% (record high) against Broadcom's 48.6%, and return on invested capital is 105% for Nvidia against 26% for Broadcom, though Broadcom's should climb toward 40% on its custom-chip backlog with Alphabet and OpenAI. The demand backdrop is hyperscaler capex: the five big US hyperscalers (Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Oracle, Meta) will have spent over $900bn in 2026 and he estimates over $1.1tn in 2027, with replacement upgrades for data centres built in 2023-24 extending demand, plus possible new catalysts in physical AI, healthcare and consumer agents. On valuation, Nvidia's fair value is $297 against about $147 (forward PE 8.9x) and Broadcom's is $450 against about $291 (forward PE 9.6x). Calls: NVDA BUY reiterated (prior BUY 24 Nov) and AVGO BUY reiterated (prior BUY 19 Nov), with Nvidia his pick - 'much more undervalued' than Broadcom. He owns both as large positions. Bear case for both: leadership turmoil, SEC and government probes, circular-financing scrutiny, and the AI cycle peaking in one to two years.

calls.bear_case: Leadership turmoil, SEC/government probes and circular-financing scrutiny weigh; the cycle peaks in 1-2 years and growth flatlines.
